title.narrative: Gateway to Nature: Caribbean Biodiversity Investment Programme

description.narrative: The Action, Gateway to Nature, intends to demonstrate that the European Union Global Gateway strategy can besuccessfully applied to environment conservation and restauration and that it can be instrumental to attract investmentin the Caribbean. It also fulfils the Global Gateway Investment Agenda (GGIA) for the Caribbean, and in particularfor the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS), which included biodiversity among its priority areas.Biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration in the Caribbean still largely rely on non-profit approaches. Yet,there is strong potential to link biodiversity to key economic sectors like tourism and food systems. The overallobjective of the Action is to strengthen the link between biodiversity and socio-economic development, drawing onEU best practices and directly engaging the EU private sector. The programme aims to prove that nature-positivebusiness models are not only sustainable but profitable, offering replicable solutions to scale impact. The GlobalGateway strategy offers a unique opportunity to engage the European private sector in promoting regenerativebioeconomy and innovative tourism investments in the Caribbean.The Specific objective of the Action is to make nature-positive investments more sustainable, integrated in nationaland regional markets and supported by innovative financing mechanisms. It targets businesses and projects that worktowards the conservation, restoration of biodiversity and changes in production methods, highlighting the region'simperative need to balance ecological preservation with economic growth.Concretely, the Action will support 5-7 high impact pilot projects with seed funding and business developmentsupport through the Caribbean Climate Smart Accelerator Innovation Fund while expanding on other sources of cofinancing.In parallel, it will support local policy developments required to facilitate nature-positive privateinvestment and the integration of the selected projects into national biodiversity and conservation frameworks.Additionally, it will strengthen financial sustainability for nature-positive private investments by strengthening theirintegration in relevant value chains and by developing sustainable and deforestation-free funding streams for theselected projects. In doing so, it will embody the Global Gateway through knowledge and technology transfer andprivate investment.The action deploys its investment strategy by focusing on three key pillars: fostering solutions that enhancebiodiversity, supporting companies in their transition towards reducing negative impacts, and adopting a BestPractices approach for those that substantially exceed sector norms in biodiversity preservation. This strategicstructuring is designed to engage a broad spectrum of entrepreneurial ambitions, particularly those eager to refinetheir production methods to prioritize ecological sustainability and biodiversity conservation, while climate actionremains an indirect benefit. By honing in on biodiversity, the program targets enterprises at various stages ofecological responsibility, from those seeking to integrate basic sustainable practices to those leading the charge withinnovative conservation techniques.To achieve this, the action will not only provide financial support and resources to projects but also engage in adynamic process of policy evolution and stakeholder engagement through a case-by-case approach in order to deliveron Global Gateway and the 360 approach. The action will implement a multi-sectoral approach, involving keyCaribbean organisations present in various fields of entrepreneurship, innovation and biodiversity, as the publicsector.
